title: Size Ramsey minimal graphs for uniform star forests
summary: For given graphs $G_{1}, G_{2}, \dots, G_{t}$ and $G$, let $G\rightarrow (G_{1}, G_{2}, \dots, G_{t})$ denote that each $t$-coloring of $E(G)$ yields a monochromatic copy of $G_{i}$ in color $i$ for some $i\in [t]$. The {\it size Ramsey number}, $\hat{r}(G_{1}, G_{2}, \dots, G_{t})$ is the minimum size of $G$ such that $G\rightarrow (G_{1}, G_{2}, \dots, G_{t})$. A graph $G$ is a {\it size Ramsey minimal graph} for $(G_{1}, G_{2}, \dots, G_{t})$ if $G\rightarrow (G_{1}, G_{2}, \dots, G_{t})$ and $e(G)= \hat{r}(G_{1}, G_{2}, \dots, G_{t})$.
